moduleSummary: Covers how new people get set up with the right kind of access to ECMS — both DOE staff getting internal accounts and community-based organization (CBO) or family child care network (FCCN) staff getting vendor portal logins — and how that access is kept accurate over time.
existingGuide: Partial overlap only: guide-01-vendor-site-setup-cbo.html (steps 8-9, CBO vendor portal provisioning)

scenarios.title: Confirming a System Administrator's own setup access
scenarios.description: Before making any access changes for other people, a system administrator can check that their own account has the special "System Administrator" level of access, since any setup changes they make apply system-wide for every user type.
scenarios.statusNote: Documented in the Phase 1 System Admin UAT/Training decks as a pre-setup check, but no automated test exists.

scenarios.title: Giving a vendor administrator access to specific ECMS functions
scenarios.description: A DOE system administrator can open a vendor contact's record and choose exactly which areas that person can work in — for example budgeting, invoicing, site management, or vendor management — by checking boxes for each function, rather than granting all-or-nothing access.
scenarios.statusNote: The general "Provision Contact" wizard (function selection) is shown in the existing user guide (steps 8-9) for a CBO site scenario, but the System Admin-driven, vendor-administrator-focused version of this flow (from the Contacts list rather than a Site record) is not separately tested.

scenarios.title: Choosing which sites a vendor administrator can see and manage
scenarios.description: When granting a vendor administrator access, the person setting it up also picks which specific program sites that administrator is allowed to view and work with, so access can be limited to only the locations relevant to that person.
scenarios.statusNote: Shown as its own step in both the System Admin and Vendor Admin UAT decks; no coverage found in the test suite or existing guide beyond a single-site example.

scenarios.title: A vendor administrator granting access to their own staff
scenarios.description: A CBO or FCCN vendor administrator can find one of their own staff members' contact records and set up that staff member's portal access themselves, choosing which functions (budgeting, invoicing, site management, vendor management) and which sites the staff member can use — without needing a DOE system administrator to do it for them.
scenarios.statusNote: Full workflow documented across 8 steps in the Phase 1 Vendor Admin UAT deck (from Sites list, into an Account's related Contacts, to the Provision Contact wizard); no dedicated test found.

scenarios.title: Confirming a vendor administrator's own starting access before provisioning others
scenarios.description: Before a vendor administrator can grant access to their team, they can check that their own account already has the right starting permission level, and can preview the system by temporarily viewing it as if logged in as their own vendor user.
scenarios.statusNote: Described as a pre-setup step in Phase 1 Vendor Admin training/UAT materials; distinct from the DOE-side "View as User" scenario since it is self-service for the vendor.

scenarios.title: Quickly setting up basic vendor management access for one person
scenarios.description: A simplified, shorter path exists for a vendor administrator to give one staff member just the single "Vendor Management" function (rather than the full multi-function, multi-site setup), useful for straightforward cases.
scenarios.statusNote: Distinct 4-step short-form flow shown in the Phase 1 Vendor Admin Training and Reference Manual, separate from the longer 8-step flow in the same deck.

scenarios.title: Previewing exactly what a newly set-up vendor user will see
scenarios.description: After granting someone portal access, the person who set it up can temporarily view the system exactly as that new user would see it, to confirm the right menus, quick-action buttons, and site information show up before telling the person their account is ready.
scenarios.statusNote: This "Log in to Experience as User" preview is documented and included in the existing guide (step 9) for the CBO vendor-site scenario, but not as a standalone repeatable check for other vendor types (e.g., FCCN) or internal DOE accounts.

scenarios.title: Setting up a brand-new internal DOE staff account
scenarios.description: When a new DOE employee (such as an Operations Analyst or Operations Director) joins the ECMS team, an administrator manually creates their internal account and assigns the correct job-based access level, work group memberships, and system license so the employee can immediately use the applications and records their role requires.
scenarios.statusNote: Described in Jira as a manual internal-user setup process (assigning role, license, and job-based access groups); no UAT script, training material section, or automated test specifically walks through creating an internal DOE user end-to-end.

scenarios.title: Onboarding a new CBO vendor organization from the citywide contract system
scenarios.description: New CBO vendor organizations are not entered into ECMS by hand — their basic information flows in automatically from the city's contract and vendor management system, and ECMS keeps that organization information up to date on an ongoing schedule.
scenarios.statusNote: Automated integration described in Jira as an end-to-end onboarding process; not a manual UAT scenario but worth documenting as a client-facing capability with no current test coverage.

scenarios.title: Confirming a new vendor employee's background-check clearance before granting access
scenarios.description: A new CBO or FCCN staff member cannot be given portal access until their background/employment clearance has been completed and verified through the city's employee clearance system; ECMS automatically brings in updated clearance information every day so staff records reflect the person's current clearance status.
scenarios.statusNote: Described in Jira as a daily automated data load creating/updating staff records ahead of any access being granted; no test coverage found.

scenarios.title: Finishing account setup with the employee's official city username
scenarios.description: Once a new vendor employee's clearance is verified, the administrator receives a notice with the employee's official DOE-assigned username and must add it to that person's record and turn on their ECMS access; skipping this step means the employee will not be able to log in at all.
scenarios.statusNote: Documented in Jira as a required manual step, with a known consequence (employee cannot log in) if missed; no scripted test scenario found for this step.

scenarios.title: Logging in through single sign-on with a city-issued account
scenarios.description: Vendor and DOE users log into ECMS using their existing city-issued username and password rather than a separate ECMS-only password, with the first successful login automatically creating or updating their portal account behind the scenes.
scenarios.statusNote: Single sign-on setup was reported as unreliable/inconsistent across test environments in Jira (DOEECMS-1757, blocked), and no test currently verifies first-time automatic account creation on login.

scenarios.title: Making sure a newly provisioned user can immediately see their reports and homepage
scenarios.description: When someone is newly set up with access, they should be able to see their reporting dashboards and homepage information right away, without running into a permissions error and without an administrator needing to fix it after the fact.
scenarios.statusNote: Reported as a defect in Jira (DOEECMS-1866) where reporting access was missing after standard setup; fix was in progress (Ready for QA) with no confirming test found.

scenarios.title: Making sure granting new access doesn't accidentally remove existing access
scenarios.description: When an administrator adds a new area of access for someone (for example adding budget and invoice access for a person who already handles enrollments), the system should add the new access on top of what they already have, not accidentally take away access they already had.
scenarios.statusNote: Reported as a defect in Jira (DOEECMS-1754) where granting vendor-management access removed a user's existing enrollment access; marked Ready for UAT with no confirming test found.

scenarios.title: Granting access to a family child care network (FCCN) staff member for a specific site
scenarios.description: An administrator should be able to grant an FCCN staff member access scoped to one particular site, the same way it works for CBO staff, without the setup process failing partway through.
scenarios.statusNote: Reported as a defect in Jira (DOEECMS-1770, High priority) where the setup process threw an error and could not be completed for FCCN staff; marked Ready for UAT with no confirming test found.
